reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an automated PancakeSwap front-running contract as a way to generate passive income, claiming profitable trades and that 90% of profits return to the wallet. Viewers are told to fund MetaMask, deploy the contract, send BNB to it, and activate its Action function, with frames showing deployment and wallet-confirmation interfaces. It also claims results such as several hundred BNB, an approximately 50x return, and up to 1000 BNB per day, while acknowledging possible fee losses and recommending at least 0.5 BNB in funding.

citations.quote: Today I'm gonna be going over deploying a front-running bot on PancakeSwap With the wrapped BNB pair
if you just follow the description of the video as far as downloading MetaMask and also funding it Make sure that it's connected to the Binance Smart Chain.

immediately buys and sells at profit. Current parameters of this contract is that 10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool, and automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit.
So we're going to send some funds to that contract that we just created.
But without further ado, let's go click action and that will start the contract.

opening.argument: The presentation includes material risk qualifications rather than presenting an unconditional outcome. Its description warns that a contract funded with 0.2 BNB could lose money when a targeted token has high burn fees, says the contract can waste more in fees than it makes, and recommends more funding to avoid that situation. It also limits the described deployment to Binance Smart Chain rather than Ethereum mainnet. Those conditions and warnings support a technology demonstration with disclosed operational risks, not a representation that every viewer will profit or that the process is risk-free.

citations.quote: If you fund the contract with 0.2 BNB and the bot targets another token with high burn fees the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit
I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.5 just to make sure that won't happen.
This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the profit language as if it erased the qualifications, but the same description expressly identifies burn fees, gas costs, network limitations, and a funding recommendation. The 90% statement describes the contract's stated parameter, not proof that a return is guaranteed; the material itself says the contract may lose more in fees than it makes.

citations.quote: 10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool, and automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit.
the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are warnings about conditions under which the promoted mechanism may perform poorly, not a neutral disclaimer against the solicitation. The same description still presents the contract as automatically buying and selling at profit and returning 90% to the wallet. A caveat about fees does not establish that the underlying code or claimed returns work.

citations.quote: immediately buys and sells at profit.
automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit.

opening.argument: The video's observable subject is a programming and deployment workflow. The speaker says the process involves Remix, creates a contract file, compiles it, deploys it through injected Web3, and inspects the resulting contract address. The sampled frames likewise show a code editor, compiler and deployment controls, a blockchain address page, and wallet confirmation interfaces. That is consistent with an operational technology tutorial or demonstration: it shows how a Solidity contract is configured and interacted with, while performance claims remain the presenter's reported experience rather than independently established facts.

citations.quote: Then you just follow over to Remix, which is where the window I've started up is right now.
with pragma solidity 6.6, which is the version of Remix that this was compiled in.
So we're going to deploy this to our wallet.
You can see that there's an address there now.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening's own evidence describes an executable workflow, but an executable workflow can still be instructional rather than deceptive promotion. The speaker explains contract creation, compilation, deployment, and interaction in sequence; the fact that the tutorial includes wallet confirmations does not by itself establish that viewers were deceived or that the demonstrated code failed.

citations.quote: Today I'm gonna be going over deploying a front-running bot on PancakeSwap
Let me go compile frontrunbot.
let's go click action and that will start the contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical setting does not neutralize the solicitation. The tutorial instructs viewers to fund the deployed contract and activate it, then ties that action to automated profit claims. Showing code, deployment, and wallet confirmations demonstrates operational steps, but it does not show that the promised trading behavior exists or that the claimed results are genuine.

citations.quote: the next step in this process is just funding your contract
it will then engage all the constructors that we built as far as engaging the pancake router
I've had really good luck with this.

opening.argument: The record is better characterized as an ordinary software-operation tutorial than as a classic deposit-return scheme. It shows a developer tool and a blockchain contract workflow, and it does not establish a downline, referral structure, credential collection, or personal-information request. The supplied material also does not establish that any viewer was promised a guaranteed outcome: the speaker describes personal experience and says the bot will compete with other bots, while the description acknowledges fee-related losses. The visible wallet authorization is part of the demonstrated blockchain operation, not proof of a concealed scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Then you just follow over to Remix, which is where the window I've started up is right now.
So you'll only be competing with other bots on the mempool
I've had really good luck with this.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies funding and activation, but those actions are also ordinary steps in deploying a blockchain contract. It does not show a downline, credential request, or hidden transfer mechanism. The stated returns are claims that require verification; their presence alone does not prove that the operational tutorial is a scam rather than a risky software demonstration.

citations.quote: So we're going to send some funds to that contract that we just created.
But without further ado, let's go click action and that will start the contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing features are not required for this scam pattern. The central mechanism described is precisely that viewers send BNB to a contract and activate it in expectation of automated trading profit. Wallet authorization and the funding instruction are therefore material, while the speaker's personal success claim and fee caveat do not prove the contract can perform as represented.
